chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Nu'ayn ibn Shu'ayb, from Shihab ibn 'Abd Rabbih, who said:

I asked him, 'What is the right of the wife upon her husband?' He said, 'He should satisfy her hunger, cover her private parts, and not mar her face (by neglect or harshness). When he does that, by Allah, he has fulfilled her right.'
I said, 'And the oil (for hair/body)?' He said, 'Alternately, one day and one day, no (not every day).'
I said, 'And the meat?' He said, 'Once every three days, ten times in the month, no more than that.'
I said, 'And the dye (for hair)?' He said, 'Every six months. And he should clothe her with four garments each year: two for winter and two for summer.'
And it is not fitting that your house be empty of three things: vinegar, oil, and head oil. Strengthen them with the mud (measure), for indeed I provide for my family with the mud.
And each person among them should determine their own provision. If he wishes, he eats it; if he wishes, he gives it away; if he wishes, he donates it.

And whenever there is general fruit, he should feed his family from it. And he should not fail to have an abundance of food for the two Eids (from their Eid) that he provides them with something from it which he does not provide them with on other days.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific material and financial rights of a wife upon her husband according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the specific material obligations (*haqq*) of a husband, detailing precise provisions for food, clothing, and grooming that reflect the socio-economic norms of the Imami scholarly tradition. It establishes a baseline for marital maintenance (*nafaqah*) while granting the wife autonomy over the distribution of her sustenance, thereby balancing legal duty with domestic harmony.
